title: Quran Study 51: Sura 17:59–67, Satan, Jinn Companions, and the Brewery Discovery (1990)
date_note: The filename identifies 1990, but no exact date is established.
document_summary: A composite Quran-study recording that begins with Quran 39:15–21 and the loss or growth of the soul, then develops the idea that every child has a correspondingly young jinn companion. Rashad interprets disease, starvation, and AIDS as signs of Satan's inability to govern an expanding human population and gives an extended account of how his work at Monsanto and Anheuser-Busch enabled the Quranic computer research. The group then discusses Gog and Magog, numerical speculation concerning seventeen, ongoing creation, four kinds of disasters, the admission test, David and Solomon's judgments, a child's recitation of al-Fatihah, soul assignment across families and generations, and Quran 17:59–67 concerning the cessation of earlier visible miracles, Satan's challenge, divine protection, ships, and people who remember God only in danger.

related_duplicate_sources.relationship: same Monsanto and Anheuser-Busch discovery narrative
related_duplicate_sources.note: Treat the brewery accounts as repeated movement history rather than independent proof.
The present recording gives a four-category disaster classification.
Medical claims must remain attributed and safety-qualified.

content_guidance.instruction: The recording is much broader than its filename.

content_guidance.rule: Preserve the brewery history but link duplicates
content_guidance.instruction: Repeated versions are one narrative family.

content_guidance.rule: Strongly qualify medical, childhood, and destiny claims
content_guidance.instruction: They cannot guide diagnosis or judgment.

sections.title: Satan's failing dominion, AIDS, starvation, Monsanto, Anheuser-Busch, and the miracle in a brewery

Rashad then recounts moving from Monsanto to Anheuser-Busch, initially rejecting brewery employment, working on protein extraction from yeast, and using the company's time and computers for Quranic research.
